description: Address all 6 issues from code review: non-atomic stock reservation, non-atomic shipment movements, phantom RPC, hardcoded 'current_user', RLS asymmetry on invoices, and warehouse mismatch in returns
steps: Fix issues 1+3 in orders.ts: Remove phantom increment_reserved_quantity RPC call, replace read-then-write loop with atomic UPDATE ... SET reserved_quantity = reserved_quantity + qty using .rpc or raw filter
Fix issue 2 in fulfillment.ts: Batch stock movement inserts into a single .insert() call with array, make reservation release also use arithmetic update
Fix issue 4 in SalesOrders.tsx, Invoices.tsx, Returns.tsx: Replace all 'current_user' string literals with user.id from useAuth() hook
Fix issue 5 in migration 006: Add UPDATE policy for invoices table allowing authenticated users to update payment-related fields
Fix issue 6 in returns.ts: Look up the original sales order's warehouse_id instead of accepting it from input
acceptance_criteria: No 'current_user' string literals remain in mutation calls
confirmOrder uses atomic UPDATE with arithmetic increment
shipOrder uses batch .insert() for stock movements
approveReturn looks up warehouse from original sales order
Migration includes UPDATE policy for invoices
pnpm build passes with zero TypeScript errors
verification: Run pnpm build and confirm zero errors
findings: All 6 issues fixed. Build passes (tsc -b + vite build). Used optimistic concurrency control (WHERE reserved_quantity = expected_value) since Supabase JS client does not support SQL arithmetic in SET clauses. The warehouse_id in ApproveReturnInput type is kept for backward compatibility but the service now prefers the original order warehouse. Also found and fixed 'current_user' in Payments.tsx which was not listed in the original review.
